market.summary: US equities are near record highs but churning under the surface. As of the July 15, 2026 close the S&P 500 was at 7,572.40 (+0.38%) and the Nasdaq at 26,269.23 (+0.62%), roughly half a percent below record closes, with the S&P up about 10.7% YTD and 24 all-time highs so far in 2026. Today (July 16) the tape turned mixed-to-soft: S&P -0.4% and Nasdaq -0.8% intraday as chips sold off after TSMC beat earnings but fell 4%+ on capex/margin concerns, while the Dow held up. The dominant internal story is a large rotation out of semiconductors (SOX reported down ~15% from its highs) into megacap hyperscalers (Apple at a record, MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL up ~3% on July 15). Macro crosscurrents: June CPI (July 14) and a -0.3% m/m June PPI (July 15) eased what had been Fed rate-HIKE bets, but PPI is still +5.5% y/y, June retail sales missed (+0.2% vs +0.3% consensus), and US strikes on Iran are keeping oil near recent highs. Net: index-level risk-on with low realized stress, but rotation, sticky y/y inflation, and geopolitics make it a mixed regime rather than a clean melt-up.
notes: VIX closed at 15.67 on 2026-07-15 (down ~5% on the day) and traded roughly 15.9-16.6 on July 16 — verified via Yahoo Finance/Investing.com quotes, not directly from Cboe (Cboe/FRED pages blocked direct fetch). Mid-15s-16 is below the long-run ~19-20 average: option premium is cheap, which is thin compensation for systematic sellers and relatively favorable for buyers of defined-risk long optionality — consistent with this repo's long-premium H6/H7/H8 lanes.

The AI-infrastructure trade is bifurcating, not breaking. Semis are in a real correction — SOX reported ~15% off its highs, Micron -8% on July 15, memory names (WDC, SNDK) down ~8% on July 16, and TSMC fell 4%+ despite a 77% earnings gain on margin/capex worries — with a reported $3.2T rotation out of chips into the Magnificent 7. Hyperscalers are the strong leg (Apple record high on China AI approval; MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL up ~3% July 15), and the power leg remains structurally bid: VST was named preferred power provider for the KKR/Nvidia-backed Helix venture (>$10B commitments) with Q1 revenue +43% y/y, and CEG has its 20-yr Microsoft Three Mile Island PPA plus a 10GW+ datacenter PPA pipeline, against reported ~$750B 2026 hyperscaler AI capex. For this repo's book: the capex thesis is intact but leadership has shifted within the trade — MSFT/AMZN/VST/CEG are on the favored side of the rotation while chip-adjacent story names face momentum headwinds.
2026-07-16: Retail sales, June 2026 (released; +0.2% m/m vs +0.3% consensus)
2026-08-07: Employment Situation (July 2026 jobs report), 8:30 a.m. ET

FOMC dates verified on federalreserve.gov; PPI release date verified via BLS archive URL (ppi_07152026); BLS schedule and Cboe/FRED pages returned 403 to direct fetch, so VIX and some dates rest on Yahoo/Investing/CNBC secondary quotes.
Next week (July 20-24) looks macro-light ahead of the July 28-29 FOMC; the Fed communications blackout precedes the meeting (Inference from standard blackout rules, not separately verified).
Unusual regime detail: markets had been pricing possible Fed rate HIKES before the soft June CPI/PPI prints eased those bets; PPI still +5.5% y/y, so the inflation tail is not closed ahead of FOMC.
Geopolitical overhang: reports of continued US strikes on Iran with crude near recent highs and Treasury yields rising on July 16.
Retail sales miss (+0.2% vs +0.3%) is a mild growth-side soft spot; single data point, not a trend.

MSFT.news_summary: MSFT closed July 15, 2026 at $398.70, down roughly 20% YTD and far off its 52-week high of $555.45, after two bruising weeks for enterprise software: IBM's surprise Q2 warning on July 14 (stock -25%, its worst day on record, citing customers redirecting budgets from conventional software/IT toward AI infrastructure hardware) dragged the whole software complex down, and MSFT briefly traded near $385 before recovering. Company-specific news includes a July 2 announcement of a $2.5B investment in 'Microsoft Frontier Co.', a new enterprise AI-implementation unit (shares +1.6% that day), and press reports (Fox Business, unconfirmed by Microsoft) of another layoff round of up to ~5,000-5,700 jobs across Xbox, sales, and consulting. Ahead of the July 29 FY26 Q4 report, at least three firms trimmed targets while keeping bullish ratings: Citi $620->$570 (Buy), Mizuho $515->$490 (Outperform), Argus $620->$510 (Buy), largely on anxiety over Microsoft's ~$190B calendar-2026 capex plan (~$35B above prior consensus). The FTC's broad antitrust probe into Microsoft's AI, cloud, licensing, and OpenAI relationship remains open with no announced resolution date.

catalysts.what: FY2026 Q4 earnings, after market close; call webcast 2:30pm PT (Nadella/Hood). Key items: Azure growth, Q4 capex guided to >$40B, ~$80B power-constrained Azure backlog, FY27 capex framing.
IBM formal Q2 earnings release — direct read-through for enterprise software/AI-budget-reallocation narrative that hit MSFT on July 14; a second shoe or a walk-back moves the sector.
Reported (unconfirmed by Microsoft) layoff round of up to ~5,700 jobs across Xbox/sales/consulting, said to land mid-to-late July — speculative until announced.
Announced $2.5B investment in Microsoft Frontier Co., new enterprise AI-implementation unit (already public; execution details may come on the earnings call).
FTC antitrust probe (AI, cloud, licensing, OpenAI partnership) ongoing; no scheduled decision date — timing speculative.

MSFT.move_thesis: The July 29 FY26 Q4 print is the dominant near-term catalyst and lands inside 2 weeks; with the stock at ~$399, down 20% YTD, and press reports of options markets positioning for a 'big swing' (no reliable implied-move figure was obtainable — treat magnitude as estimated), a 5-8% post-earnings move in either direction is plausible given the IBM-triggered demand doubts colliding with still-bullish sell-side positioning (average target ~$589). Upside case: Azure growth holds, the $80B power-constrained backlog converts to revenue visibility, and capex commentary reassures — a relief move retraces the July software selloff toward the pre-selloff zone and the low-$430s (roughly the Mizuho-style de-rated targets discount ~23% upside from here). Downside case: any echo of IBM's 'AI cannibalizes software budgets' message or another capex raise pushes MSFT through the $376 support cited by technicians toward the 52-week low at $349.20 (-12%). Before July 29, IBM's July 22 report is the sector tape-setter and could move MSFT 2-4% sympathetically in either direction. Note: this is Inference from levels and event positioning, not a prediction; the implied-move figure specifically could not be verified from a primary source.
MSFT.risks: The IBM warning suggests enterprise customers are actively reallocating budgets away from traditional software toward AI hardware, which threatens Microsoft's non-Azure segments (Office/Dynamics/consulting-adjacent revenue) even if Azure stays strong, and MSFT's YTD underperformance versus other Mag-7 names shows the market is already penalizing the ~$190B capex plan whose returns remain unproven. A capex increase without matching Azure acceleration on July 29 risks a break of $376 support toward the $349 52-week low, and the open FTC antitrust probe into the OpenAI relationship is an unpriced tail risk with no resolution date.

AMZN.news_summary: AMZN trades near $255 (closed $255.18 on 2026-07-15, +3.25% that day) with the story dominated by AI-infrastructure spending: on July 7 Amazon launched a $25B eight-part senior unsecured bond sale to fund AI buildout (orders peaked near $62B; ~$54B of debt raised YTD), with 2026 capex tracking toward ~$200B and trailing-12-month free cash flow collapsing to ~$1.2B from ~$25.9B a year ago. AWS grew 28% YoY in Q1 2026 ($37.6B revenue, fastest in 15 quarters, ~37.7% operating margin), helped by large Trainium deals with OpenAI (~2GW) and Anthropic (up to 5GW). Prime Day moved earlier to June 23-26 and set records (~$26.4B US e-commerce spend, +9.3% YoY), pulling the event fully into Q2 results. Analyst posture into the July 30 print is constructive: consensus is Strong Buy with an average price target around $314; TD Cowen (July 8) trimmed its target to $340 from $350 but forecasts Q2 revenue ~2% and operating income ~10% above consensus. Separately, Amazon paid $2.25M on June 30 to settle FTC Fair Credit Reporting Act claims, and the main FTC monopolization trial is now set for February 2027.

catalysts.what: Q2 FY2026 earnings after US market close (estimated - widely reported by earnings calendars and CNBC, but not verified against an Amazon IR press release; street: ~$196B revenue, ~$1.82 EPS; company guide $194-199B sales, $20-24B op income)
$25B bond sale for AI infrastructure priced (completed; company indicated no further 2026 debt issuance)
FCC deadline for Amazon Leo (ex-Kuiper) to deploy 1,600 satellites; only ~700 expected deployed, 24-month extension requested - regulatory decision pending
FTC v. Amazon monopolization bench trial start (amended scheduling order; outside the 2-month options window but a standing overhang)
FTC FCRA settlement, $2.25M civil penalty (closed item, minor)

AMZN.move_thesis: The dominant near-term event is the July 30 Q2 report: options are pricing an earnings reaction of roughly +/-7.05% (~$17.37), implying a post-print range of about $238-$273 from the ~$255 spot (Options AI / OptionCharts, mid-July reading). The bull path runs through AWS re-acceleration (28% in Q1, TD Cowen modeling Q2 revenue ~2% and operating income ~10% above consensus) plus the record Prime Day landing entirely in Q2, which could push the stock toward the low-$270s and, over weeks, toward the ~$314 consensus target. The bear path is a repeat of the capex/FCF shock narrative: with TTM free cash flow at ~$1.2B and ~$200B capex, a Q3 capex guide-up or any AWS margin compression could dominate a headline beat and drive the stock toward the ~$238 implied-move floor or the upper-$220s. Between now and the print, the $25B bond deal is already digested and no comparable scheduled catalysts remain, so drift plus IV build into July 30 is the base case; the FCC Leo deadline on the same day is a minor secondary headline risk.
AMZN.risks: Free cash flow has collapsed to ~$1.2B TTM against ~$200B capex, and the debt-funded AI buildout (~$54B raised YTD, priced with extra yield concession per Fortune) makes the stock acutely sensitive to any wobble in AI-demand or AWS margin narrative on the call. Prime Day data showed softer per-household spend ($143.45 vs $156.37) and lower deal satisfaction, so the retail beat may be lower quality than the headline record implies. The FTC monopolization trial (Feb 2027) and the pending FCC Leo satellite-deadline decision are standing regulatory overhangs.

VST.news_summary: Vistra confirmed via a July 6, 2026 press release that it will report Q2 2026 results on Friday, Aug 7, 2026 (10 a.m. ET call). On July 14, 2026 it filed an 8-K disclosing PJM 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction results: ~10,924 MW cleared at a weighted average of $325.00/MW-day, with the RTO price again at the FERC-approved cap and PJM reporting its first-ever RTO-wide reliability shortfall (6,831 MW short, 138,318 MW procured). Shares rose ~4.1% on July 6 to $153.43 and were up roughly 12% over the prior month, trading near $158 into mid-July; on July 15 shares added ~1.1% after an analyst action, with Scotiabank reportedly raising its target to $298 (Sector Outperform). Backdrop remains the nuclear/datacenter PPA story: the Meta 20-year deals (Perry/Davis-Besse ~2,176 MW plus Beaver Valley uprates, announced January 2026, Perry delivery starting December 2026) and the September 2025 AWS 1,200 MW Comanche Peak PPA (delivery from Q4 2027).

catalysts.what: Q2 2026 earnings + conference call 10 a.m. ET (company-confirmed; consensus EPS ~$2.43 per aggregators, labeled aggregator-estimated)
PJM 2028/2029 capacity auction results (just occurred): Vistra cleared ~10,924 MW at $325.00/MW-day weighted average; RTO cleared at FERC cap, first-ever RTO-wide shortfall
Perry nuclear Meta PPA delivery begins December 2026 (part of 20-yr Meta deals announced Jan 2026: Perry/Davis-Besse 2,176 MW + Beaver Valley uprates)
AWS Comanche Peak 1,200 MW 20-yr nuclear PPA, initial delivery Q4 2027; company says up to ~3.2 GW additional capacity potentially available at Beaver Valley/Comanche Peak for future deals
SPECULATIVE: additional data-center/co-location PPA announcements (management has said it is engaged in co-location discussions; no date or counterparty confirmed)

VST.move_thesis: The dominant near-term vol event is Q2 earnings on Aug 7, 2026, ~3 weeks out and inside any 1-2 month option tenor; aggregators cite consensus EPS ~$2.43 with one preview flagging a ~140% YoY EPS jump, and VST has a history of large single-day earnings reactions (inference from its high-beta merchant-power profile, not a measured statistic). The July 14 PJM print ($325/MW-day at the cap, first-ever RTO shortfall) was absorbed as mildly positive (+1.1% on July 15 alongside a target raise) — it locks in 2028/29 capacity revenue visibility but was largely expected since this is the third consecutive cap-clearing auction and the price is actually -2.5% YoY, so it is unlikely to drive further large upside alone. With the stock near $158 vs. $153.43 on July 6, aggregator consensus targets in the low-to-mid $200s (TipRanks avg ~$225, low $181, 13 buys/0 holds/0 sells) and a fresh Scotiabank high target of $298 (both aggregator-reported, not independently verified), the sell-side skew is strongly bullish; a beat-and-raise or a new hyperscaler PPA headline plausibly supports a move toward the $170s-$180 (the lowest published target), i.e. high-single to low-double-digit percent upside over 1-2 months. Absent a new catalyst, drift risk is toward the $150-153 area where the pre-PJM/pre-earnings-announcement price sat.
VST.risks: Earnings is a two-sided event: merchant generators' quarterly results are hedge-book and weather sensitive, and a miss or soft commentary near all-time-high analyst expectations (zero holds/sells) leaves little cushion — a give-back toward $150 or below is plausible on a bad print. The PJM 2028/29 price came in -2.5% YoY and future auctions face political/regulatory pressure on the price cap, capping the capacity-revenue growth narrative. The datacenter-PPA premium embedded in the stock is vulnerable to any cooling in AI-power headlines or delays in Perry/Davis-Besse delivery milestones; note this name sits inside the owner's concentrated AI/semis/power factor.

CEG.news_summary: CEG has had a volatile two weeks: on July 1, 2026 Citi cut its price target to $297 from $348 (Neutral) and the stock fell ~5% to a fresh 52-week low of $228.63. It then rebounded roughly 7% after PJM's 2028/29 Base Residual Auction results were released July 14: prices hit the $325/MW-day cap and Constellation disclosed via 8-K that it cleared 18,875 MW (15,700 MW nuclear, 3,175 MW fossil/other), worth an estimated ~$2.2B in capacity revenue for the 2028/29 delivery year. This follows the June 1 FERC waiver letting Constellation transfer 760 MW of Eddystone interconnection rights to the Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island-1), keeping the Microsoft-backed 835 MW restart on its 2027 timeline instead of ~2031. Calpine integration (deal closed Jan 7, 2026) continues, including the agreed PJM generation asset sale to LS Power required by the FERC/DOJ resolution. As of July 16, 10:25 AM ET the stock trades ~$252.45 (down ~2.2% on the day), about 39% below its 52-week high of $412.70 and down ~26% YTD.

catalysts.what: Q2 2026 earnings conference call, 10:00 AM ET (company IR, confirmed)
PJM 2028/29 capacity auction results: CEG cleared 18,875 MW at the $325/MW-day price cap, ~$2.2B capacity revenue (already occurred; earnings-call quantification pending)
Crane Clean Energy Center (TMI-1, 835 MW) restart targeted 2027; June 1, 2026 FERC waiver preserved the timeline; NRC milestones and restart-progress updates are ongoing catalysts
Additional data-center co-location/PPA announcements expected through 2026 (management-signaled, e.g. Calpine sites after the Feb 9 CyrusOne Freestone 380+380 MW deal) — speculative timing, no dates
Closing of PJM generation asset sale to LS Power (required by FERC/DOJ Calpine resolution) — announced, closing timing unconfirmed

CEG.move_thesis: The one scheduled near-term event is the confirmed Q2 earnings call on 2026-08-06 (inside 3 weeks and well inside the 2-month options window); CEG's recent single-day moves around news have been large (-5% on the July 1 Citi cut, ~+7% on the July 14 PJM auction print), so a 5-8% one-day move around earnings is plausible in either direction. Upside path: management quantifying the cap-priced PJM auction (~$2.2B for 2028/29) into guidance, plus any new hyperscaler co-location PPA, could carry the stock from ~$252 toward the $290-$300 area (Citi's reduced $297 target is the low end of the analyst range; consensus PT is ~$372 per TipRanks as of July 10). Downside path: a guidance disappointment or Calpine integration/cost surprise retests the $228.63 52-week low, ~9% below current levels. Unscheduled data-center deal announcements are the main asymmetric bull catalyst — prior comparable announcements moved the stock high-single-digits in a day — but their timing is speculative.
CEG.risks: The stock is in a persistent 2026 downtrend (-26% YTD, 39% off highs) with a fresh Citi Neutral/$297 cut citing valuation, so positive news has recently been sold into strength. Calpine ($16.4B+ deal) integration risk, the mandated PJM asset divestiture to LS Power, and any Crane restart slippage (2027 target depends on remaining NRC/execution milestones) are concrete bear catalysts. PJM capacity revenue at the $325 cap is also politically sensitive — consumer-cost backlash in Pennsylvania and other PJM states raises regulatory-intervention risk to future auction pricing.
